name: John N. Kennedy
role: U.S. senator from Louisiana (Republican, 2017-present); Louisiana State Treasurer (2000-2017)
summary: Louisiana Republican senator, a former Democrat (switched 2007), who combines fiscal hawkishness, opposition to abortion, gun-rights advocacy and support for oil, gas and nuclear energy with a populist, anti-bureaucracy tone. He backs Israel, Ukraine aid with oversight, a hard line on China and Iran, and tough border and crime policy, and he generally favours reducing tariffs while backing Trump's leverage on trade.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted in 2017 to repeal the Affordable Care Act, calling it a failure, and has pushed Medicaid work requirements; he has not backed state-guaranteed universal coverage.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: As a 2004 Democratic candidate he backed raising the federal minimum from $5.15 to $6.65; in a 2016 Senate survey he opposed a livable-wage question. Evidence from different periods points both ways and no recent statement was found.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Repeatedly argues for competition and market choice (school choice, "may the best, cheapest product win" on trade) and against government interference in exchange.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Led floor arguments for extending the 2017 tax cuts, called the alternative a $4.3 trillion tax increase and voted for the 2025 reconciliation bill that made them permanent.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mostly pushes to cut regulation (BLOCK Act, CRA resolutions on bank-merger and energy rules, LNG permits), but also backed net neutrality and says regulators failed to enforce existing rules; mixed record leans toward less regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Says there are too many "undeserving people at the bottom getting handouts", calls Medicaid work requirements a way out of "poverty and dependency", but says Medicaid spending still grows under his bill.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Opposed marijuana legalization in a 2016 candidate survey and is described by NORML as outspoken against it; no recorded support for legalizing other recreational drugs.

state-harmful.rationale: States that the first purpose of government is protecting people and property and defends police, courts and punishment, which rejects the idea that the state is unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Writes that "We don't need stricter gun laws", holds an A+ NRA rating, led CRA resolutions against an ATF rule and signed on to concealed-carry reciprocity.

empower-police-military.rationale: Says Congress must increase defense spending because "weakness invites the wolves", and argues that many colleagues wrongly treat police as a bigger problem than criminals.

decide-locally.rationale: Says education and abortion policy should return to the states and that what is good in Louisiana differs from other states, but also backs national measures (SAVE Act, federal abortion bills).

rehabilitation.rationale: Voted against the First Step Act calling it a prisoner release bill, and says people who hurt others must be punished and, if repeat offenders, separated from society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against the Respect for Marriage Act while noting that same-sex marriage is legal under Obergefell and the bill was unnecessary; earlier cosponsored FADA and backed a man-woman marriage definition in a 2016 survey.

abortion-legal.rationale: Strongly pro-life: cosponsor of the Life at Conception Act and multiple abortion restrictions; called Roe a legal and moral error.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Argues sex differences are biological ("biological men", "biological women") and opposes irreversible gender procedures for minors.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposes illegal immigration and sought to end the diversity visa lottery, but says legal immigration makes the country better; no stated target level.

free-trade.rationale: Says tariffs interfere with freedom to exchange and urges zero tariffs so "the best product at the best price win"; also accepts leverage tariffs against China.

nation-first.rationale: Says America First "does not have to be me in America alone" and wants allies, while demanding reciprocal trade and NATO burden sharing; mixed.

open-borders.rationale: Backs a border wall, ending sanctuary cities and criminal penalties for visa overstays; accused the Biden administration of an open-border policy.

limit-growth.rationale: Argues the economy must grow and that expiring tax cuts would send GDP "to the center of the Earth"; opposes growth-limiting climate policy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls Biden climate agenda ruinous for jobs and seeks to block fossil-fuel limits; his own climate measure was a narrow HFC phase-down framed around jobs.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Wrote that nuclear power is a safe, carbon-free source that America should expand, including small modular reactors, alongside fossil fuels.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Says tariffs put a thumb on the scale and an eye-for-an-eye leaves both blind, while crediting Trump for pressing China; supports reducing tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Voted against the CHIPS Act, calling it a subsidy to Big Tech and the Inflation Reduction Act as a tax-and-spend bill.

one-party-rule.rationale: Said "I believe in a two-party system" because competition makes everyone better.

military-superiority.rationale: Says Congress must increase defense spending because Xi, Putin and Iran's rulers must not become the world's policemen, and calls nuclear modernization a top priority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Calling the US a nation of immigrants is nearby; no stated position on ethnic composition of a nation.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Support for Israel's self-defence is nearby; no stated position on a Jewish state in the Land of Israel.

school-vouchers.rationale: Supports vouchers, charters and parental choice and praised the school-choice funding in the 2025 reconciliation bill.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted against the 2021 American Rescue Plan as pork and says deficit spending must stop, though he backed the emergency CARES Act and a 2020 relief bill.

force-without-un.rationale: Backing strikes without mentioning the UN is not a stated position on UN approval.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Introduced and campaigned for SNAP and Medicaid work requirements and welcomed them in the 2025 law.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Op-eds and bills defend and expand oil, gas and LNG production and exports and seek to overturn drilling bans.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Criticism of Washington and particular elites is nearby; no broad stated position.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Says government's "first" purpose is to protect people and property but supports many other functions (education funding, insulin cap, disaster aid).

separated-powers.rationale: Frequently invokes checks and balances: introduced the BLOCK Act to return rulemaking to Congress and defends the filibuster and judicial restraint.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Says "America First does not have to be me in America alone", wants friends abroad, criticizes European allies for not backing the Iran strikes, and opposes giving up the Diego Garcia base.

death-penalty.rationale: As a candidate called the 2008 Supreme Court ruling against the death penalty for child rape "morally reprehensible" and a "wrong-headed, left-wing, activist decision".

religious-exemptions.rationale: Cosponsored the First Amendment Defense Act, which shields people from federal penalties for religious beliefs about marriage.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Backed the 2025 rescission of foreign aid programs and argues countries should fund their own priorities.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Calls modernizing and expanding the U.S. nuclear stockpile a top priority.

no-bailouts.rationale: Said "too many undeserving people at the top" get bailouts and called the 2023 rescue of three banks a bailout that taxpayers ultimately fund.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Defends the Constitution's difficult Article V amendment path and proposed an amendment fixing court size; strongly defends the Second Amendment.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Introduced a bill to bar airlines from putting pets in overhead bins after a dog died.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Introduced the CONFUCIUS Act, cutting federal funds to colleges that do not control foreign-government-funded Confucius Institutes.

non-intervention.rationale: Backed U.S. strikes on Iran, the Venezuela operation, and aid to Ukraine including seizing Russian assets.

religion-illusion.rationale: Speaks of faith and prays; said unborn children are "formed in the hand of God".

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Calls for higher defense spending and a bigger nuclear arsenal.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Backs NATO and Taiwan deterrence and says "America First does not have to be America alone", rejecting neutrality.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Challenged a witness who had reposted "abolish the police" and says wrongdoers must be punished and, if repeat offenders, separated from society; voted against the First Step Act.

term-limits.rationale: Cosponsored a constitutional amendment limiting House members to three terms and senators to two.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Opposing foreign nationals voting in federal elections is nearby; local elections not addressed.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Says "I believe love is the answer, but I also own a handgun, just in case," and defends gun ownership for self-defence.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Writes that men and women differ biologically and refers to "biological men" and "biological women".

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Op-ed treats women as a biological category when defending women's sports.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Called the U.S. and Israeli attack on Iran "the right thing" to stop its nuclear program and backed forceful responses to adversaries.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Opposed a proposed $900-per-ton methane fee as harmful to energy producers and consumers.

arms-reduction.rationale: Wants the U.S. to modernize and expand its arsenal and boost defense spending rather than cut arms.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Cosponsored a balanced budget constitutional amendment (two-thirds vote for tax increases, spending capped at 18% of GDP).

student-debt-relief.rationale: Opposed Biden's plan ("On what planet is that fair?") and celebrated the Supreme Court striking it down.

public-service-media.rationale: Argued on the Senate floor that Congress should stop funding NPR, PBS and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and backed the rescission.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Argues the stockpile is old and shrinking and that the U.S. must produce more plutonium pits to deter China, Russia, North Korea and Iran.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Introduced a bill lowering the fentanyl quantity that triggers a mandatory minimum sentence.

voter-id.rationale: Supports the SAVE America Act "unconditionally," which requires proof of citizenship to register and identification to vote.

close-ties-china.rationale: Hawkish on China: introduced Taiwan sanctions, CONFUCIUS Act and delisting bills against Chinese firms.

notes: Switched from Democrat to Republican in August 2007; his 2004 Senate campaign positions (e.g. raising the minimum wage) predate that switch and were not treated as current. Statements read from senate.gov were fetched through Internet Archive copies because the live site blocks automated access.
